# load required packages

```{r}

Sys.setenv(TZ='GMT')

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# The COAPS/FSU SAMOS true-wind algorithm (Smith & Bourassa, samos@coaps.fsu.edu),
# vendored unmodified. Supplies truew(), which the Meteorology section uses to
# correct the ship-relative wind. See R/tw.R.
source(here("R", "tw.R"))

```

# helpers

```{r}

# Cruise the raw logs belong to. Prefixes every file written to output/, and
# selects the cruise's input directory: its raw logs, and its event log. Set
# SHARP_CRUISE in the environment, or edit this line.
cruise <- tolower(Sys.getenv("SHARP_CRUISE", unset = "hrs2606"))

# Every plot in this notebook is QC, not a product: nothing written to output/
# depends on one. They are the bulk of the runtime (they roughly quadruple it),
# so they are off unless asked for -- set SHARP_PLOTS=1 in the environment, or
# edit this line, to get the QC report back.
make_plots <- identical(Sys.getenv("SHARP_PLOTS", unset = "0"), "1")

# Wrap every QC plot in qc(). The argument is a lazy promise, so when plotting is
# off the plot is never built at all. ggplot objects have to be printed to draw;
# base graphics (hist) draw as a side effect of being forced, so print only the
# ggplots and hand the rest back invisibly.
qc <- function(expr) {
  if (!make_plots) return(invisible(NULL))
  x <- expr
  if (inherits(x, "ggplot")) print(x)
  invisible(x)
}

# Zero-line reference: the clockwise angle from the bow to the anemometer's zero
# line, needed to turn ship-relative wind into true wind. 0 means the zero line
# is the bow, which is the normal meaning of the "R" (relative) reference field
# the RM Young puts in its $WIMW sentences.
#
# CAVEAT: 0 is an assumption. It has NOT been confirmed with the R/V Sharp that
# either anemometer is aligned to the bow. If the ship reports an offset, set
# SHARP_ZLR to it. A wrong zlr rotates true wind direction by exactly that many
# degrees and leaves true wind speed almost untouched, so it is not self-evident
# in the output -- the wind1-vs-wind2 QC plot at the end of the Meteorology
# section is the check that would catch the two masts differing from each other.
zlr <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("SHARP_ZLR", unset = "0"))

# Root of this cruise's raw instrument logs: one subdirectory per instrument,
# each holding its own raw/ (input/hrs2606/raw/gps01/raw/HS2606EM_gps01-...).
# Cruises accumulate side by side under input/, so adding one is dropping a
# directory in, not editing this notebook. The logs are large; SHARP_RAW_ROOT
# points at a cruise's raw/ kept outside the project.
raw_root <- Sys.getenv("SHARP_RAW_ROOT", unset = here("input", cruise, "raw"))

if (!dir.exists(raw_root)) {
  stop("raw log directory not found: ", raw_root,
       "\nUnpack ", cruise, "'s raw logs there, or set SHARP_RAW_ROOT to ",
       "their location.")
}

# `cruise` now picks the directory as well as labelling the output, so the two
# can no longer drift apart the way they could when every cruise shared one
# input/raw. What is left to catch is misfiling: another cruise's logs sitting
# in this cruise's directory. The ship names every file for the cruise it
# recorded (HS2606EM_gps01-2026-07-09), so take that number back out of the
# filenames and require the whole directory to agree on one.
#
# The number the ship writes is not always the cruise's own -- HRS2601's logs
# are all labelled HS2501, the previous year's number, which the ship's logger
# was never updated from. So a label that disagrees with the directory is a
# mislabel and warns; two different labels in one directory is genuinely mixed
# data and stops.
#
# PAR is logged by Biospherical's software rather than the ship's, and its
# filenames carry only a date (BSI20260423_145702.csv). There is nothing in them
# to check a cruise against, so they sit out of this. See process_par.R.
cruise_num <- str_extract(cruise, "\\d+")
raw_files  <- basename(dir(raw_root, recursive = TRUE))

if (length(raw_files) == 0) {
  stop("no raw log files found under: ", raw_root)
}

ship_num   <- str_match(raw_files, "^HS(\\d{4})")[, 2]
ship_found <- unique(ship_num[!is.na(ship_num)])

if (length(ship_found) > 1) {
  stop("logs from more than one cruise are mixed together under ", raw_root,
       ": the ship labelled some HS", paste(sort(ship_found), collapse = ", HS"),
       ".\nEach input/<cruise>/ directory holds one cruise's logs.")
}
if (length(ship_found) == 0) {
  warning("none of the ", length(raw_files), " files under ", raw_root,
          " are ship logs named HS<cruise>_<instrument>-<date>, so there is ",
          "nothing to check \"", cruise, "\" against. First: ", raw_files[1])
} else if (ship_found != cruise_num) {
  warning("cruise is \"", cruise, "\", but the ship labelled these logs HS",
          ship_found, ". Taking input/", cruise, "/ as authoritative and ",
          "proceeding -- this is expected for hrs2601, whose logs are all ",
          "HS2501. Check the directory if it is not.")
}

# Products are written here; keep them out of the raw tree.
out_dir <- here("output")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Every product is named <cruise>_<what>.csv.
product <- function(what) file.path(out_dir, paste0(cruise, "_", what, ".csv"))

# Only <cruise>_underway_noPAR.csv is the product. The other nine files are
# intermediates: the partially-joined underway tables, the full-rate $PASHR and
# $INVTG dumps, and the standalone 1-minute per-instrument files. They are useful
# for QC and for reproducing the products that predate the met work, but they are
# not what gets published, so they are not written unless asked for --
# set SHARP_INTERMEDIATES=1 in the environment, or edit this line.
write_intermediates <- identical(Sys.getenv("SHARP_INTERMEDIATES", unset = "0"), "1")

# Use for every file that is not the final product. Returns its input invisibly,
# so it can sit in a pipeline without breaking it.
write_intermediate <- function(df, what) {
  if (write_intermediates) write_csv(df, product(what))
  invisible(df)
}

# Raw instrument files are NMEA-style: each line is a timestamped sentence with
# comma- or tab-separated fields. Field count varies by sentence type, so the
# files cannot be handed to read_csv() directly -- split a character vector of
# already-filtered lines into a fixed number of columns instead.
split_fields <- function(lines, field_names, delim = ",") {
  m <- str_split_fixed(lines, stringr::fixed(delim), length(field_names))
  df <- as_tibble(m, .name_repair = "minimal")
  colnames(df) <- field_names
  df
}

read_all_lines <- function(instrument) {
  paths <- dir(file.path(raw_root, instrument, "raw"), full.names = TRUE)
  unlist(lapply(paths, read_lines), use.names = FALSE)
}

# The leading field of every sentence is "<ISO8601 timestamp> $XXYYY"; the
# timestamp occupies the first 27 characters.
iso_from_field <- function(x) str_sub(x, 1, 27)

parse_iso <- function(x) as.POSIXct(x, tz = "GMT", format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")

# NMEA degrees-minutes: DDMM.MMMM (lat) or DDDMM.MMMM (lon), no separator,
# with the hemisphere in a following field.
dm_to_decimal <- function(x, hemi, deg_digits) {
  deg <- as.numeric(str_sub(x, 1, deg_digits))
  min <- as.numeric(str_sub(x, -7))
  (deg + min / 60) * if_else(hemi %in% c("S", "W"), -1, 1)
}

# The published files timestamp every row as UTC with an explicit offset.
iso_offset <- function(x) paste0(format(x, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "+00:00")

# Subsample an instrument onto a 1-minute grid by taking the first sample in
# each minute. Where a sample lands in the boundary second this is identical to
# the old filter(second(datetime) == 0); where instrument clock drift means no
# sample landed there, it fills the minute instead of dropping it -- which is
# what the hand-built *_seconds_corr.csv patches used to do.
# tol_sec caps how stale a filled value may be; minutes whose first sample is
# further out than that are dropped rather than carried.
snap_to_minute <- function(df, tol_sec = 30) {
  df |>
    mutate(minute = floor_date(datetime, "minute")) |>
    group_by(minute) |>
    slice_min(datetime, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(as.numeric(difftime(datetime, minute, units = "secs")) <= tol_sec)
}

# The raw NMEA fields carry signed zeros ("-0.00"), which R keeps as -0 and
# write_csv renders as "-0". Collapse them onto positive zero.
zap_neg_zero <- function(x) if_else(x == 0, 0, x)

# NMEA checksum: XOR of every character between the "$" and the "*", compared
# against the two hex digits after the "*". A serial dropout mid-sentence still
# yields a parseable line with plausible-looking numbers in it, so the met
# sentences below are checked before they are trusted. Sentences repeat heavily
# at 1 Hz, so checksum only the distinct ones and look the rest up.
nmea_ok <- function(lines) {
  m     <- str_match(lines, "\\$([^*]*)\\*([0-9A-Fa-f]{2})\\s*$")
  body  <- m[, 2]
  given <- m[, 3]

  ok   <- rep(FALSE, length(lines))  # unparseable => bad
  have <- !is.na(body)
  u    <- unique(body[have])
  sums <- vapply(u, \(s) Reduce(bitwXor, as.integer(charToRaw(s))), integer(1))
  ok[have] <- sprintf("%02X", sums[match(body[have], u)]) == toupper(given[have])
  ok
}

# Wind direction is a bearing, so it cannot be averaged as a scalar: the mean of
# 359 and 1 is 180, not 0. Resolve each sample into a vector, average those, and
# take the bearing back out. Speed is reported as the scalar mean (the usual met
# convention) rather than the length of the mean vector, which would be damped
# by any veering within the averaging window.
avg_wind <- function(df, unit, prefix) {
  df |>
    group_by(datetime = floor_date(datetime, unit = unit)) |>
    summarize(
      u        = mean(wind_speed * sin(wind_dir * pi / 180)),
      v        = mean(wind_speed * cos(wind_dir * pi / 180)),
      speed_kt = mean(wind_speed),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(rel_dir_deg = (atan2(u, v) * 180 / pi) %% 360) |>
    select(datetime, rel_dir_deg, speed_kt) |>
    rename_with(\(x) paste0(prefix, "_", x), c(rel_dir_deg, speed_kt))
}

# Correct one anemometer's ship-relative wind to true wind -- the direction the
# wind blows FROM referenced to true north, and its speed over the fixed earth --
# by subtracting out the ship's own motion. Adds <prefix>_true_dir_deg and
# <prefix>_true_speed_kt, and leaves the relative columns in place.
#
# The vector math is truew() from R/tw.R. cspd and wspd have to be in the same
# units, and truew() does not convert: both are knots here (sog_kts from $INVTG,
# and $WIMW reports knots), so true speed comes out in knots too. Do not hand it
# sog_kmh. wdir has to be meteorological -- the direction the wind comes FROM --
# which is what $WIMW already reports, so it goes in as-is.
#
# North comes back as 360, not 0, whenever the wind is blowing: that is truew()
# honoring the WMO convention, and it is left alone.
true_wind <- function(df, prefix, zlr_deg = zlr, wmis = DEFAULT_MISSING_VALUES) {
  crse <- df$course_true_deg
  cspd <- df$sog_kts
  hd   <- df$heading
  wdir <- df[[paste0(prefix, "_rel_dir_deg")]]
  wspd <- df[[paste0(prefix, "_speed_kt")]]

  # truew() needs a heading referenced to true north. Refuse to compute rather
  # than quietly hand it a magnetic one.
  hd[!df$heading_type %in% TRUE] <- NA_real_

  # $INVTG leaves course blank when the ship is not making way, so a stopped ship
  # has speed 0 and no course. Course only ever reaches the math as
  # cspd * cos(course), which is 0 for any course once cspd is 0 -- so fill a
  # course in rather than throw the record away. (A course missing while the ship
  # IS moving stays missing, and the row goes to NA below.)
  crse[is.na(crse) & !is.na(cspd) & cspd == 0] <- 0

  # truew() cannot see NA -- an NA reaching one of its range checks aborts the
  # call -- so missingness has to travel as the sentinel values it was written to
  # recognize. Note wmis is ordered c(crse, cspd, wdir, wspd, hd), which is NOT
  # the argument order of truew() itself.
  na_to <- function(x, sentinel) if_else(is.na(x), sentinel, as.numeric(x))
  crse <- na_to(crse, wmis[1])
  cspd <- na_to(cspd, wmis[2])
  wdir <- na_to(wdir, wmis[3])
  wspd <- na_to(wspd, wmis[4])
  hd   <- na_to(hd,   wmis[5])

  # One row at a time, via truew() rather than its truewinds() wrapper: every
  # setting of truewinds()' `sel` argument, including the one documented as
  # silent, prints a diagnostic table, which would land in the knitted report.
  tw <- pmap(
    list(crse = crse, cspd = cspd, wdir = wdir, hd = hd, wspd = wspd),
    \(crse, cspd, wdir, hd, wspd) truew(crse = crse, cspd = cspd, wdir = wdir,
                                        zlr = zlr_deg, hd = hd, wspd = wspd,
                                        wmis = wmis)
  )
  tdir <- map_dbl(tw, "tdir")
  tspd <- map_dbl(tw, "tspd")

  # A missing or out-of-range record comes back as the sentinel, never as NA.
  # Sentinels must not reach the product.
  df[[paste0(prefix, "_true_dir_deg")]]  <- if_else(tdir == wmis[3], NA_real_, tdir)
  df[[paste0(prefix, "_true_speed_kt")]] <- if_else(tspd == wmis[4], NA_real_, tspd)
  df
}

```

# GPS

```{r}

GGA_COLS <- c("datetime_type","GPSTime","Latitude","NorS","Longitude","EorW",
              "FixQuality","NumSats","HDOP","AntennaHeight","UnitsAntennaHeight",
              "GeoidHeight","UnitGeoidHeight","ow","CheckSum")

gps01 <- read_all_lines("gps01") |>
  str_subset("GGA,") |>
  split_fields(GGA_COLS) |>
  mutate(
    datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime_type),
    datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO),
    FixQuality  = as.numeric(FixQuality),
    dec_lat     = dm_to_decimal(Latitude, NorS, 2),
    dec_lon     = dm_to_decimal(Longitude, EorW, 3)
  )

# check fix quality
#  from Definitions.txt: "0=invalid, 1=GPS, 2=DGPS, 3=PPS, 4=RTK, 5=Float RTK"
qc(hist(gps01$FixQuality))

gps01 <- gps01 |> select(datetimeISO, datetime, dec_lat, dec_lon)
gps01$dec_lat <- round(gps01$dec_lat, 5)
gps01$dec_lon <- round(gps01$dec_lon, 5)

qc(ggplot(gps01, aes(x = datetime, y = dec_lat))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(gps01, aes(x = datetime, y = dec_lon))+geom_point())

# The event log is a cruise-level product, not raw instrument output, so it sits
# beside the cruise's raw/ rather than inside it (input/hrs2606/R2R_ELOG_...).
# It is only ever overlaid on the track plots, so it is not read at all when
# plotting is off, and a missing one is not an error. Its full name carries a
# timestamp that cannot be guessed
# (R2R_ELOG_HRS2606HS_FINAL_EVENTLOG_20260427_160219.csv), so match on the
# stable part of the name inside the cruise's own directory -- staging one
# cruise's event log for another is then not possible by accident.
elog_dir  <- here("input", cruise)
elog_path <- dir(elog_dir, pattern = "EVENTLOG.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE,
                 ignore.case = TRUE)

elog <- if (!make_plots) {
  NULL
} else if (length(elog_path) == 1) {
  read_csv(elog_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
} else if (length(elog_path) > 1) {
  warning("more than one event log in ", elog_dir, " -- skipping elog overlays: ",
          paste(basename(elog_path), collapse = ", "))
  NULL
} else {
  message("no event log matching *EVENTLOG*.csv in ", elog_dir,
          " -- skipping elog overlays")
  NULL
}

if (!is.null(elog)) {
  qc(ggplot(elog, aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude))+geom_point())
  qc(ggplot(gps01, aes(x = dec_lon, y = dec_lat))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = elog, aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude), color = "blue3"))
}

```

```{r}
# reduce data set to 1-minute timestamps

# Position is instantaneous, not averaged: take the first fix in each minute.
# datetimeISO keeps the true sample time; datetime carries the grid boundary.
# Logging starts mid-minute, so the opening grid minute is only partly covered
# -- and the averaged channels joined onto it below would average a short
# window. Start the spine at the first minute the instrument was already
# running for.
first_full_minute <- ceiling_date(min(gps01$datetime), "minute")

gps01_1min <- gps01 |>
  snap_to_minute() |>
  mutate(datetime = minute) |>
  filter(datetime >= first_full_minute) |>
  select(datetimeISO, datetime, dec_lat, dec_lon)

qc({
  p <- ggplot(gps01_1min, aes(x = dec_lon, y = dec_lat))+geom_point()
  if (!is.null(elog)) p <- p + geom_point(data = elog, aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude), color = "blue3")
  p
})

write_intermediate(gps01_1min, "gps_1minute")

```

# Fluorometer

```{r}

FLUOR_COLS <- c("datetime","time","ChlChannel","ChlCount","TurbChannel","TurbCount","Auxiliary")

# Using FLNTU characterization sheet date March 6, 2026, S/N FLNTURT-090
# chl
## Scale factor 0.0121 ug/L/count
## Dark counts = 50 counts
## chl (ug/L) = scale factor x (output - dark counts)
# turb
## Scale factor = 0.0061 NTU/count # NTU = nephelometric turbidity unit
## Dark counts = 50 counts
## NTU = scale factor x (output - dark counts)

fluor <- read_all_lines("flnturt") |>
  split_fields(FLUOR_COLS, delim = "\t") |>
  mutate(
    datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime),
    datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO),
    ChlCount    = as.numeric(ChlCount),
    TurbCount   = as.numeric(TurbCount),
    chl_ugl     = 0.0121 * (ChlCount - 50),
    turb_ntu    = 0.0061 * (TurbCount - 50)
  ) |>
  select(-time) |>
  relocate(datetimeISO, .before = datetime)

qc(ggplot(fluor, aes(x = datetime, y = chl_ugl))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(fluor, aes(x = datetime, y = turb_ntu))+geom_point())

# calculate 1-minute average of chlorophyll and turbidity
fluor_avg <- fluor |>
  group_by(datetime = floor_date(datetime, unit = "minutes")) |>
  summarize(across(c(chl_ugl, turb_ntu), mean), .groups = "drop")

fluor_avg$chl_ugl <- round(fluor_avg$chl_ugl, 2)
fluor_avg$turb_ntu <- round(fluor_avg$turb_ntu, 2)

# match 1-minute average to 1-minute instantaneous coordinates
underway <- left_join(gps01_1min, fluor_avg, by = "datetime")

# plot averaged timeseries
qc(ggplot(underway, aes(x = datetime, y = chl_ugl))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(underway, aes(x = datetime, y = turb_ntu))+geom_point())

```

# Thermosalinograph

```{r}

TSG_COLS <- c("datetime","cond","sal")

tsg <- read_all_lines("sbe4501") |>
  split_fields(TSG_COLS) |>
  mutate(
    # the temperature is appended to the leading timestamp field
    temp        = as.numeric(str_sub(datetime, -7)),
    datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime),
    datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO),
    cond        = as.numeric(cond),
    sal         = as.numeric(sal)
  )

# calculate 1-minute average of temperature, conductivity, salinity
tsg_avg <- tsg |>
  group_by(datetime = floor_date(datetime, unit = "minutes")) |>
  summarize(across(c(temp, cond, sal), mean), .groups = "drop")

tsg_avg$temp <- round(tsg_avg$temp, 3)
tsg_avg$cond <- round(tsg_avg$cond, 3)
tsg_avg$sal <- round(tsg_avg$sal, 3)

# match 1-minute average to 1-minute instantaneous coordinates
underway <- left_join(underway, tsg_avg, by = "datetime")

# plot raw data
qc(ggplot(tsg, aes(x = datetime, y = temp))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(tsg, aes(x = datetime, y = cond))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(tsg, aes(x = datetime, y = sal))+geom_point())

# plot averaged timeseries
qc(ggplot(underway, aes(x = datetime, y = temp))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(underway, aes(x = datetime, y = cond))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(underway, aes(x = datetime, y = sal))+geom_point())

```

# Read the POS files once and pull out both sentence types of interest.

pos_lines <- read_all_lines("pos")

PASH_COLS <- c("datetime_type","time","heading","heading_type","roll_deg","pitch_deg",
               "heave_m","RollAccuacy","PitchAccuracy","HeadingAccuracy","IMUStatus","CheckSum")

VTG_COLS <- c("datetime_type","courseTrue","courseTypeT","courseMag","courseTypeM",
              "speedKt","speedTypeNaut","speedKm","speedTypeKM","CheckSum")

pash <- pos_lines |> str_subset(".PASHR,.") |> split_fields(PASH_COLS)
vtg  <- pos_lines |> str_subset(".INVTG,.") |> split_fields(VTG_COLS)

unique(pash$IMUStatus) # "2" "0" "1"

write_intermediate(pash, "pash")
write_intermediate(vtg, "vtg")

```{r}
# format pash

pash <- pash |>
  mutate(
    type        = str_sub(datetime_type, -7),
    datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime_type),
    datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO),
    # PASHR reports heading relative to true north; the published column is a flag
    heading_type = heading_type == "T"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(heading, roll_deg, pitch_deg, heave_m, IMUStatus),
                \(x) zap_neg_zero(as.numeric(x)))) |>
  select(-datetime_type, -time, -CheckSum) |>
  relocate(datetimeISO, datetime, .before = heading)

# decided not to use averaging

pash_1min <- pash |> snap_to_minute() |> mutate(datetime = minute)

unique(pash_1min$IMUStatus) #2

pash_1min <- pash_1min |> select(datetime, heading, heading_type, roll_deg, pitch_deg, heave_m)

```

```{r}
# join with other 1-min data

# The published datetimeISO identifies the $INVTG sample, so it is picked up
# from the vtg join below rather than carried over from the GPS fix.
underway_p <- underway |>
  select(-datetimeISO) |>
  left_join(pash_1min, by = "datetime") |>
  relocate(date, .before = dec_lat)

write_intermediate(underway_p, "underway_noMet_noPAR_pash")

```

```{r}

# format vtg

vtg <- vtg |>
  mutate(
    type        = str_sub(datetime_type, -7),
    datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime_type),
    datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(courseTrue, courseMag, speedKt, speedKm), as.numeric))

# decided not to use averaging

qc(ggplot(vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = courseTrue))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = courseMag), color = "blue3"))

qc(ggplot(vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = speedKt))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = speedKm))+geom_point())

vtg_1min <- vtg |>
  snap_to_minute() |>
  mutate(datetime = minute) |>
  select(datetimeISO, datetime, courseTrue, speedKt, speedKm)

write_intermediate(vtg_1min, "vtg_1min")

qc(ggplot(vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = courseTrue))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = vtg_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = courseTrue), color = "blue3"))

qc(ggplot(vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = speedKt))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = vtg_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = speedKt), color = "blue3"))

qc(ggplot(vtg, aes(x = datetime, y = speedKm))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = vtg_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = speedKm), color = "blue3"))

```

```{r}

# join with other 1-min data

# snap_to_minute() emits one row per minute boundary, so the hand-built
# hrs2601_{pash,vtg}_seconds_corr.csv patches are no longer needed. These
# should both be 0.
sum(duplicated(vtg_1min$datetime))
sum(duplicated(underway_p$datetime))

underway_p <- underway_p |>
  filter(!is.na(heading)) |>
  arrange(datetime)

underway_v <- left_join(underway_p, vtg_1min, by = "datetime")
sum(duplicated(underway_v$datetime))

# check for minutes present in the position spine but missing a speed
underway_v_check <- filter(underway_v, is.na(speedKt))
nrow(underway_v_check)

# compare heading variables, heading true from pash lines and course true from vtg lines
qc(ggplot(underway_v, aes(x = datetime, y = heading))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = underway_v, aes(x = datetime, y = courseTrue), color = "blue3"))
# These track each other closely, but they are not the same variable and both are
# published: heading is where the bow points, course is where the ship actually
# goes, and the difference between them is the crab angle the ship carries under
# wind and current. The true wind correction in the Meteorology section needs
# both, and publishing course is what lets a downstream user reproduce it.

underway_v <- underway_v |>
  rename(course_true_deg = courseTrue, sog_kts = speedKt, sog_kmh = speedKm) |>
  relocate(date, datetimeISO, .before = dec_lat) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), zap_neg_zero))

# `date` carries the grid minute in the published files; `datetime` is the join
# key the met section below still needs, so it is dropped on the way out only.
write_intermediate(underway_v |> select(-datetime), "underway_noMet_noPAR")

```

# Meteorology

```{r}

# The RM Young logs three sentences, each at 1 Hz:
#   $WIMW1,<dir>,R,<speed>,N,A   wind sensor 1 -- direction and speed
#   $WIMW2,<dir>,R,<speed>,N,A   wind sensor 2 -- direction and speed
#   $WIXDR,C,<temp>,C,TEMP,H,<rh>,%,RH,P,<baro>,hPa,BARO
#
# Wind is logged relative to the ship (the "R" reference field): the direction is
# a bearing off the bow, not off true north, and it is not corrected for the
# ship's own heading and speed here. Speed is in knots (the "N" units field).
#
# Unlike the other instruments, the met stream is checksummed before use -- see
# nmea_ok() above.

met_lines <- read_all_lines("rmyoung")

met_ok <- nmea_ok(met_lines)
message(sum(!met_ok), " of ", length(met_lines), " met sentences failed checksum")
met_lines <- met_lines[met_ok]

MW_COLS  <- c("datetime_type","wind_dir","dir_ref","wind_speed","speed_units","status")

XDR_COLS <- c("datetime_type","t_type","air_temp","t_units","t_id",
              "h_type","rel_hum","h_units","h_id",
              "p_type","baro","p_units","p_id")

# The sensor signs directions just to port of the bow ("-00", "-01"), so wrap the
# bearing back into [0, 360). avg_wind() below is indifferent to this -- sin and
# cos do not care -- but the full-rate values written out should not be negative.
read_wind <- function(lines, sensor) {
  lines |>
    str_subset(paste0("\\$WIMW", sensor, ",")) |>
    split_fields(MW_COLS) |>
    mutate(
      datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime_type),
      datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO),
      wind_dir    = as.numeric(wind_dir) %% 360,
      wind_speed  = as.numeric(wind_speed)
    ) |>
    # status "A" (valid) has the checksum still attached to it; "V" would be void
    filter(str_starts(status, "A"), !is.na(datetime), !is.na(wind_dir), !is.na(wind_speed)) |>
    select(datetimeISO, datetime, wind_dir, wind_speed)
}

wind1 <- read_wind(met_lines, 1)
wind2 <- read_wind(met_lines, 2)

xdr <- met_lines |>
  str_subset("\\$WIXDR,") |>
  split_fields(XDR_COLS) |>
  mutate(
    datetimeISO = iso_from_field(datetime_type),
    datetime    = parse_iso(datetimeISO),
    air_temperature_degree_c  = as.numeric(air_temp),
    relative_humidity_percent = as.numeric(rel_hum),
    barometric_pressure_hpa   = as.numeric(baro)
  ) |>
  select(datetimeISO, datetime, air_temperature_degree_c,
         relative_humidity_percent, barometric_pressure_hpa)

# plot raw data
qc(ggplot(wind1, aes(x = datetime, y = wind_speed))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = wind2, aes(x = datetime, y = wind_speed), color = "blue3"))
qc(ggplot(wind1, aes(x = datetime, y = wind_dir))+geom_point()+geom_point(data = wind2, aes(x = datetime, y = wind_dir), color = "blue3"))
qc(ggplot(xdr, aes(x = datetime, y = air_temperature_degree_c))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(xdr, aes(x = datetime, y = relative_humidity_percent))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(xdr, aes(x = datetime, y = barometric_pressure_hpa))+geom_point())

```

```{r}

# calculate 1-minute average of wind, air temperature, humidity, pressure

met_1min <- avg_wind(wind1, "minute", "wind1") |>
  full_join(avg_wind(wind2, "minute", "wind2"), by = "datetime") |>
  full_join(
    xdr |>
      group_by(datetime = floor_date(datetime, unit = "minutes")) |>
      summarize(across(c(air_temperature_degree_c, relative_humidity_percent,
                         barometric_pressure_hpa), mean), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "datetime"
  ) |>
  arrange(datetime)

# The met sensor runs on the dock before the GPS does, so this covers more
# minutes than the underway spine; the join below keeps only the overlap.
write_intermediate(
  met_1min |> mutate(date = iso_offset(datetime)) |> relocate(date) |> select(-datetime),
  "met_1min"
)

# round met parameters
met_1min$air_temperature_degree_c <- round(met_1min$air_temperature_degree_c, 1)
met_1min$relative_humidity_percent <- round(met_1min$relative_humidity_percent, 0)
met_1min$barometric_pressure_hpa <- round(met_1min$barometric_pressure_hpa, 0)

# plot averaged timeseries
qc(ggplot(met_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = wind1_speed_kt))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(met_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = wind1_rel_dir_deg))+geom_point())
qc(ggplot(met_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = air_temperature_degree_c))+geom_point())

```

```{r}

# join with other 1-min data

underway_m <- left_join(underway_v, met_1min, by = "datetime")

# every minute of the spine should have met on it
sum(is.na(underway_m$air_temperature_degree_c))
sum(duplicated(underway_m$datetime))

# The wind the anemometers report is the wind the ship feels, which is the real
# wind plus the ship's own motion through it. Subtract the ship back out to get
# the wind an observer standing still would have measured. Both sensors are
# corrected; each keeps its relative columns alongside its true ones.
underway_m <- underway_m |>
  true_wind("wind1") |>
  true_wind("wind2") |>
  relocate(wind1_true_dir_deg, wind1_true_speed_kt, .after = wind1_speed_kt) |>
  relocate(wind2_true_dir_deg, wind2_true_speed_kt, .after = wind2_speed_kt)

# When the ship is not moving there is nothing to subtract, so true wind must
# collapse to the relative wind simply rotated onto true north. That is the one
# case with a closed-form answer, so check it against one: this should be 0.
underway_m |>
  filter(sog_kts == 0, heading_type) |>
  mutate(
    dir_err = abs(((wind1_true_dir_deg - (heading + wind1_rel_dir_deg + zlr)) %% 360 + 180) %% 360 - 180),
    spd_err = abs(wind1_true_speed_kt - wind1_speed_kt)
  ) |>
  summarize(n = sum(!is.na(dir_err)),
            max_dir_err = max(c(0, dir_err), na.rm = TRUE),
            max_spd_err = max(c(0, spd_err), na.rm = TRUE))

# datetime (the POSIXct minute grid) is kept on underway_m past this point: it is
# the join key the PAR section below needs. It is dropped on the way out of each
# product write instead. zap_neg_zero only touches numeric columns, so the
# POSIXct key rides through untouched.
underway_m <- underway_m |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), zap_neg_zero))

# round wind parameters
underway_m$wind1_rel_dir_deg <- round(underway_m$wind1_rel_dir_deg, 0)
underway_m$wind1_true_dir_deg <- round(underway_m$wind1_true_dir_deg, 0)
underway_m$wind1_speed_kt <- round(underway_m$wind1_speed_kt, 1)
underway_m$wind1_true_speed_kt <- round(underway_m$wind1_true_speed_kt, 1)

underway_m$wind2_rel_dir_deg <- round(underway_m$wind2_rel_dir_deg, 0)
underway_m$wind2_true_dir_deg <- round(underway_m$wind2_true_dir_deg, 0)
underway_m$wind2_speed_kt <- round(underway_m$wind2_speed_kt, 1)
underway_m$wind2_true_speed_kt <- round(underway_m$wind2_true_speed_kt, 1)

# The two anemometers see the same wind, so their true winds should scatter about
# the 1:1 line. What to look for is a *constant rotational offset* between them,
# which is the signature of the two masts having different zero lines.
#
# Do not read the raw spread as an error in the correction. The two sensors
# disagree in true direction by a bit more than they do in relative direction,
# and that is geometry, not a bug: converting to true winds rescales the wind
# vector by (apparent speed / true speed), so a fixed disagreement between the
# sensors is amplified whenever the ship is steaming into the wind and damped
# whenever it is running with it. Speed, which is not rescaled that way, does
# agree more closely in true coordinates than in relative.
qc(ggplot(underway_m, aes(x = wind1_true_dir_deg, y = wind2_true_dir_deg))+geom_point(alpha = 0.2)+geom_abline(slope = 1, color = "blue3")+coord_fixed())
qc(ggplot(underway_m, aes(x = wind1_true_speed_kt, y = wind2_true_speed_kt))+geom_point(alpha = 0.2)+geom_abline(slope = 1, color = "blue3")+coord_fixed())

# True vs relative over the cruise: the correction should be largest when the
# ship is fastest, and the two should converge as it slows.
qc(ggplot(underway_m, aes(x = datetimeISO |> parse_iso()))+geom_point(aes(y = wind1_rel_dir_deg), color = "grey60")+geom_point(aes(y = wind1_true_dir_deg))+labs(x = "datetime", y = "wind1 direction (grey = relative, black = true)"))
qc(ggplot(underway_m, aes(x = datetimeISO |> parse_iso()))+geom_point(aes(y = wind1_speed_kt), color = "grey60")+geom_point(aes(y = wind1_true_speed_kt))+labs(x = "datetime", y = "wind1 speed, kt (grey = relative, black = true)"))

# datetimeISO carries the $INVTG sample time as the raw NMEA ISO string
# ("2026-07-09T21:13:00.291129Z"). Downstream parses the published timestamps as
# "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%z", which has no place for the T, the Z, or the sub-second,
# so render datetimeISO in the same space+offset form as `date`. Done here, after
# the QC plots above that still parse the raw T...Z form via parse_iso(), and
# once -- the second-level sample time survives; only the fractional second, which
# the downstream format cannot represent, is dropped.
underway_m <- underway_m |>
  mutate(datetimeISO = iso_offset(parse_iso(datetimeISO)))

# The underway product without PAR: position, chl, turbidity, T/C/S, attitude,
# course, speed, and met -- with wind reported both relative to the ship and true.
# PAR is joined onto this spine in the section below; this file is the deliverable
# whenever the PAR logs have not arrived yet. `datetime` is the PAR join key and
# is dropped on write.
write_csv(underway_m |> select(-datetime), product("underway_noPAR"))

```

# PAR

```{r}

# The PAR channel is logged by Biospherical's LoggerLight software rather than by
# the ship's underway system, so it arrives separately and in its own format --
# but it is filed as one more instrument under the cruise
# (input/<cruise>/raw/par/raw/BSI*.csv), beside the ship's own logs. It is joined
# onto the underway spine built above to produce the full <cruise>_underway.csv.
#
# PAR often arrives after the rest of the cruise has been processed. When its logs
# are not there yet this section does nothing but say so: underway_noPAR.csv above
# is the deliverable until PAR shows up, and re-knitting once it has adds
# par_1min.csv and underway.csv.

par_root <- Sys.getenv("SHARP_PAR_ROOT",
                       unset = here("input", cruise, "raw", "par", "raw"))

# PAR is filed as one more instrument under the cruise, beside gps01 and rmyoung,
# even though Biospherical's logger wrote it rather than the ship's underway
# system, so `cruise` picks these logs the same way it picks the notebook's. The
# BSI filenames carry a date and no cruise number, so they sit out of the
# HS<cruise> cross-check in the helpers section.
par_paths <- if (dir.exists(par_root)) {
  dir(par_root, pattern = "^BSI.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
} else {
  character()
}

have_par <- length(par_paths) > 0

if (!have_par) {
  message("no BSI*.csv PAR logs under ", par_root,
          " -- has ", cruise, "'s PAR data arrived yet? ",
          "Skipping PAR; ", basename(product("underway_noPAR")),
          " is the product until it has.")
}

# A LoggerLight file is a fixed 8-line header block, a column header, then 5-second
# samples:
#
#   LoggerLight version 1.3.1, 4/23/2026 14:57:02, interval  5sec, Warning: ...
#   System S/N: QSR - S/N 10367, calibrated: 1/1/2022. Tag ,"2"
#   ScaleFactor,604.71,,,,,,
#   Offset+FO,0.193502,,,,,,
#   Units,Einsteins/m2/s,,,,,,
#   Immersion,n/a,,,,,,
#   Cal Date,1/1/2022,,,,,,
#   Tag Address,2,,,,,,
#   Time,QSR - S/N 10367,Minimum,Maximum,StDev,Integral,#Averaged,
#   4/23/2026 14:57:05,1.234567E-03,...
#
# ScaleFactor and Offset+FO are reported for provenance; LoggerLight has already
# applied them, which is why the Units line reads Einsteins and not counts. Do not
# apply them again. The header is located by finding the "Time," line rather than
# by skipping 8 lines, so a logger writing a longer or shorter preamble on a later
# cruise still parses.
PAR_HEADER_RE <- "^Time,"

# The Units line contains a superscript 2 (Einsteins/m^2/s), a single byte in the
# logger's cp1252 output and invalid UTF-8. Read as cp1252 so the line does not
# come back mangled or abort the read.
read_par_file <- function(path) {
  lines <- read_lines(path, locale = locale(encoding = "cp1252"),
                      progress = FALSE)

  hdr_i <- which(str_detect(lines, PAR_HEADER_RE))[1]
  if (is.na(hdr_i)) {
    stop("no column header (a line starting \"Time,\") in: ", basename(path))
  }

  meta   <- lines[seq_len(hdr_i - 1)]
  fields <- str_split_fixed(lines[hdr_i], stringr::fixed(","), 8)

  # Field 2 of the header names the probe -- "QSR - S/N 10367" on HRS2601. Read
  # rather than hardcoded so a cruise that ships a different probe does not
  # silently produce an all-NA column.
  sensor <- fields[2]

  # Pull a value out of the "Key,value,,,,,," metadata lines.
  meta_value <- function(key) {
    hit <- str_subset(meta, paste0("^", key, ","))
    if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    str_trim(str_split_fixed(hit[1], stringr::fixed(","), 3)[2])
  }

  # Samples are the 8-field lines. LoggerLight also writes bare 2-field status
  # messages into the data block ("All statistics reset.", "Program closed
  # normally.", "Sampling resumed after manual pause"), which carry a timestamp
  # and prose where the reading should be. Drop and count them.
  body <- lines[-seq_len(hdr_i)]
  body <- body[str_trim(body) != ""]

  m    <- str_split_fixed(body, stringr::fixed(","), 8)
  time <- str_trim(m[, 1])
  # Field 2 is the reading. Anything non-numeric there is a status message.
  value <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m[, 2]))
  is_sample <- !is.na(value)

  tibble(
    file        = basename(path),
    sensor      = sensor,
    scale_factor = meta_value("ScaleFactor"),
    units       = meta_value("Units"),
    cal_date    = meta_value("Cal Date"),
    n_messages  = sum(!is_sample),
    time        = time[is_sample],
    par_native  = value[is_sample]
  )
}

```

```{r}

# Everything below is guarded on the PAR logs being present, so the notebook knits
# to underway_noPAR.csv when they are not.
if (have_par) {

  par_raw <- bind_rows(lapply(par_paths, read_par_file))

  # One probe per cruise. Two would mean logs from different deployments (or
  # different cruises) mixed together in par_root, and averaging across them would
  # be meaningless.
  sensors <- unique(par_raw$sensor)
  if (length(sensors) > 1) {
    stop("more than one PAR probe among the logs under ", par_root, ": ",
         paste(sensors, collapse = ", "),
         "\nSeparate the deployments and run them one at a time.")
  }

  # Calibration and scaling are what turn the counts into the published number, so
  # a change in either mid-cruise silently changes the units of half the product.
  if (length(unique(par_raw$scale_factor)) > 1) {
    warning("ScaleFactor is not the same in every log: ",
            paste(unique(par_raw$scale_factor), collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (length(unique(par_raw$cal_date)) > 1) {
    warning("Cal Date is not the same in every log: ",
            paste(unique(par_raw$cal_date), collapse = ", "))
  }

  # The conversion below is a unit change, not a calculation, and only valid
  # because the logger says it is emitting Einsteins. Refuse to guess otherwise.
  # Match loosely: the superscript 2 does not survive every encoding, and
  # "Einsteins/m2/s" and "Einsteins/m^2/s" are the same units.
  units_native <- unique(par_raw$units)
  if (!all(str_detect(units_native, regex("einstein", ignore_case = TRUE)))) {
    stop("PAR logs are not in Einsteins -- the Units line reads: ",
         paste(units_native, collapse = ", "),
         "\nThe umol/m2/s conversion below assumes Einsteins/m2/s.")
  }

  message(length(par_paths), " PAR logs, probe ", sensors,
          ", ScaleFactor ", unique(par_raw$scale_factor),
          ", calibrated ", unique(par_raw$cal_date))
  # n_messages is a per-file count carried on every one of that file's rows, so it
  # has to be de-duplicated before it is summed.
  n_dropped <- par_raw |> distinct(file, n_messages) |> pull(n_messages) |> sum()
  message(n_dropped, " logger status messages dropped; ",
          nrow(par_raw), " samples read")

  # LoggerLight timestamps are M/D/YYYY H:M:S with no zero padding and no zone.
  #
  # The zone is the load-bearing assumption: nothing in the file says UTC, and a
  # logger left on ship-local time would put every reading four hours off the
  # underway spine -- an error that would survive the join looking perfectly
  # plausible. The diel cycle in the HRS2601 logs confirms UTC: PAR peaks near
  # 16:30-17:00 in logger time, which is solar noon in UTC at the shelf-break
  # longitude (12:00 + 70 deg / 15 = ~16:40), not the ~12:40 a logger on EDT would
  # show. The par_diel QC plot below is what rechecks this for a new cruise.
  par_all <- par_raw |>
    mutate(
      datetimeISO = time,
      datetime    = as.POSIXct(time, tz = "GMT", format = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S"),
      # Einsteins (= mol photons) to umol, the conventional PAR unit.
      par_umol_m2_s = par_native * 1e6
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(datetime)) |>
    arrange(datetime) |>
    select(file, datetimeISO, datetime, par_native, par_umol_m2_s)

  if (nrow(par_all) == 0) stop("no PAR samples parsed -- check the Time format")

  message("PAR spans ", format(min(par_all$datetime)), " to ",
          format(max(par_all$datetime)), " UTC")

  # plot raw data
  qc(ggplot(par_all, aes(x = datetime, y = par_umol_m2_s))+geom_point()+labs(y = "PAR, umol/m2/s"))

  # The timezone check described above, drawn: PAR against hour of day. The
  # daylight lobe must be centered near 16-17 UTC. Centered near 12-13 instead
  # means the logger clock is on ship-local time and the UTC assumption is wrong.
  qc(ggplot(par_all, aes(x = hour(datetime) + minute(datetime)/60, y = par_umol_m2_s))+
       geom_point(alpha = 0.1)+
       geom_vline(xintercept = 16.7, color = "blue3")+
       labs(x = "hour of day, logger clock", y = "PAR, umol/m2/s",
            title = "diel cycle (blue = solar noon in UTC at ~70W)"))

  # calculate 1-minute average of PAR
  #
  # PAR is a continuous scalar, so it is averaged over the minute like chl,
  # turbidity and T/C/S above -- not subsampled with snap_to_minute() like the
  # instantaneous channels (position, attitude, course). The logger's 5-second
  # cadence is not phase-locked to the minute and re-phases after every "All
  # statistics reset", so averaging (rather than an exact-timestamp match) uses all
  # ~12 samples in the minute and fills every minute the logger was running.
  par_1min <- par_all |>
    group_by(datetime = floor_date(datetime, unit = "minutes")) |>
    summarize(par_umol_m2_s = mean(par_umol_m2_s),
              n_samples     = n(),
              .groups = "drop")

  # ~12 samples per minute at the 5-second logging interval. Short minutes bracket
  # a logger restart and are expected; counted, not dropped, because a mean of even
  # one sample is still that minute's PAR.
  qc(ggplot(par_1min, aes(x = n_samples))+geom_bar()+labs(x = "samples per minute"))
  message(sum(par_1min$n_samples < 6), " of ", nrow(par_1min),
          " minutes built from fewer than 6 samples (restarts and log boundaries)")

  # The logger is stopped and restarted through the cruise, so the 1-minute series
  # has real holes. Report them rather than pad them: a minute with no PAR must
  # reach the product as NA, which the join below does by leaving it out.
  gaps <- par_1min |>
    mutate(gap_min = as.numeric(difftime(datetime, lag(datetime), units = "mins"))) |>
    filter(gap_min > 1)
  message(nrow(gaps), " gaps in the 1-minute PAR series",
          if (nrow(gaps) > 0) paste0(" (longest ", round(max(gaps$gap_min)), " min)") else "")
  if (nrow(gaps) > 0) print(gaps |> select(resumes_at = datetime, gap_min))

  qc(ggplot(par_1min, aes(x = datetime, y = par_umol_m2_s))+geom_point()+labs(y = "PAR, umol/m2/s"))

  # write the 1-minute PAR file
  par_out <- par_1min |>
    mutate(date = iso_offset(datetime)) |>
    select(date, par_umol_m2_s)
  write_csv(par_out, product("par_1min"))
  message("wrote ", product("par_1min"), " (", nrow(par_out), " minutes)")

  # join PAR onto the underway spine
  #
  # A left_join onto the spine on the minute grid, exactly as the fluorometer and
  # TSG are joined above. underway_m still carries `datetime` (its date and
  # datetimeISO columns are already finished strings), so the join reformats
  # nothing and drops the join key on the way out.
  underway_par <- underway_m |>
    left_join(par_1min |> select(datetime, par_umol_m2_s), by = "datetime") |>
    select(-datetime)

  # The PAR logger runs on its own schedule -- typically starting before the cruise
  # and stopping partway through it -- so minutes of the spine with no PAR are
  # normal. A spine with NO PAR at all is not: that is the signature of a timezone
  # or cruise mismatch, where the two series simply never overlap.
  n_missing <- sum(is.na(underway_par$par_umol_m2_s))
  if (n_missing == nrow(underway_par)) {
    stop("the join produced no PAR at all: the underway spine (",
         format(min(underway_m$datetime)), " to ", format(max(underway_m$datetime)),
         ") and the PAR logs (", format(min(par_all$datetime)), " to ",
         format(max(par_all$datetime)), ") do not overlap.",
         "\nAre both from ", cruise, "?")
  }
  message(n_missing, " of ", nrow(underway_par),
          " underway minutes have no PAR")

  write_csv(underway_par, product("underway"))
  message("wrote ", product("underway"))
}

```
